policy: Evals never consume backlog issues. Any live run that implements an issue uses a dedicated eval issue created for the run — title prefixed 'eval:', body marked experimental, labeled 'eval' — or an issue the user explicitly names. After the run: the PR is CLOSED, never merged, by anyone, at any time; the branch is deleted locally and on origin; every eval issue is closed. Nothing from an eval run stays in a review queue.

evals.expected_output: Agent resolves the target, reads it, discovers the open blocker named in its body, and stops at the gate: reports what blocks with state and link, takes nothing (no assignment, no branch, no Projects Status, no codegraph index).
assertions: Does not assign the user to the target issue when stopping on a blocker — assignment (step 6) follows the blocker gate
Sets no Projects Status: the board is untouched when the run stops at the gate (step 10 is never reached)
Final report names the blocking issue as an open blocker, with its state and link, and what must land first
Stops without implementing: no new branch or worktree created and no source files modified
No Codegraph index is built on a blocked stop (step 5 is past the gate; a status check is allowed)

evals.prompt: pick up an issue from the backlog and work on it
evals.expected_output: Agent lists open issues with gh issue list and asks the user to choose. Does not pick an issue on its own, does not start implementing.
assertions: Lists open issues via gh issue list before any implementation action
Final output asks the user to choose an issue
Does not assign itself to any issue and creates no branch or worktree

evals.prompt: run the do-gh-issue-v2 skill end-to-end for the dedicated eval issue #<n> created for this run
evals.expected_output: Full v2 pipeline against a dedicated eval issue: implementation commit, refactor pass (own commit if adopted), PR before gating with uncommented Closes #<n>, gate push with intent and skip as push options from a pane running the TUI dashboard, yolo engaged once via footer-verified toggle, terminal outcome via axi status, branch_sync-aware sync, final handoff, two-part report-back, then full cleanup (PR closed — never merged — branch deleted, eval issue closed).
assertions: Uses only the dedicated eval issue (title 'eval: …', labeled 'eval') — no backlog issue is assigned, branched, or implemented
Creates a branch named <n>-<slug> from origin/<default-branch> (exact convention, no prefixes or suffixes)
Implementation is committed before the refactor pass runs, so refactor changes form their own commit on top (and no empty refactor commit when nothing was adopted)
The refactor-change-set pass runs over the full change set and its adopted/rejected lists are recorded
A PR exists on the branch before the first git push no-mistakes, and its body contains an uncommented 'Closes #<n>' line

The gate push runs in a separate Herdr pane and carries BOTH push options: -o no-mistakes.intent=<base64 of 'issue title + flattened issue body + implementation decisions'> (the gate decodes it — plain text fails the hook and no pipeline starts) and -o no-mistakes.skip=pr
After wait-output 'Pipeline started', the pane runs 'no-mistakes attach' — the TUI dashboard, not TOON axi output

Yolo is engaged exactly once via the verify-then-send protocol: footer read shows 'y yolo' → single 'herdr pane send-keys <pane> y' (pane run cannot drive the TUI) → footer confirms 'end yolo'; no blind second send is ever made
After engagement the agent only polls axi status from its own shell (no further pane keys) until the terminal outcome
The terminal outcome is confirmed via no-mistakes axi status from the agent's own shell, not from the pane transcript
Post-outcome sync follows the branch_sync.next_action.code reported by axi status (sync/recover_custody/continue_active_run/user_owned each acted on correctly)
Final handoff contains the Refactor-change-set subsection (adopted + rejected) and the Pipeline line with the outcome and PR URL
Both host-pane reports arrive: PR URL right after the PR opens, and the outcome line after the handoff
Cleanup: the PR is CLOSED (never merged — no merge command or merge action anywhere), the branch is deleted locally and on origin, and the eval issue is closed

evals.prompt: run the do-gh-issue-v2 skill end-to-end for the dedicated eval issue #<n>, where your Herdr environment check evaluates to unset (simulate with env -u HERDR_ENV when evaluating and running the gate path)
evals.expected_output: Agent detects the missing Herdr environment at step 17, warns, and drives the gate blocking in its own shell: push with the same -o options, then no-mistakes axi run --skip pr --yes (non-interactive). No herdr commands anywhere. Same dedicated-eval-issue policy and full cleanup.
assertions: Detects the missing Herdr environment at step 17 (HERDR_ENV check evaluated under env -u HERDR_ENV) rather than attempting herdr commands blindly
Prints a warning naming the missing Herdr environment before falling back
Makes no herdr calls (no pane split, no pane run, no pane read) anywhere in the run
Still pushes through the no-mistakes gate with the -o intent and skip=pr push options and drives axi run --skip pr --yes blocking in its own shell, to a terminal outcome confirmed via axi status
Uses only a dedicated eval issue and performs the full cleanup: PR closed (never merged), branch deleted locally and on origin, eval issue closed
